title: When Iteration Cannot Help: Single-Pass Missing-Modality\\ MRI Synthesis and What Actually Limits It
abstract: Missing-modality MRI synthesis predicts an unavailable contrast from the remaining acquisitions, for which diffusion-based approaches often require hundreds or thousands of network evaluations per volume. We investigate when such iterative refinement can help in informed-prior bridges and show that, when the source state is a deterministic function of the conditioning, subsequent states cannot provide additional target information. However, stochastic training states expose the network to information unavailable during inference, creating a mismatch between training and deployment. To address this, we introduce PRIMED, a single-pass displacement regression framework that trains exclusively at the source endpoint and synthesises the missing contrast with one network evaluation. A single shared network handles all four target contrasts using a fixed 3D Haar wavelet representation. On BraTS-GLI, PRIMED achieves 28.56~dB PSNR and 0.944 SSIM in 0.152~s per volume, exceeding its two-evaluation bridge by 0.596~dB at half the runtime and achieving higher PSNR than thousand-step cWDM at comparable SSIM, with a $1{,}053\times$ speedup. Its effectiveness is further validated on unseen BraTS cohorts and a separately trained IXI setting. Beyond synthesis performance, we investigate the information limits of missing-modality reconstruction, finding that recoverability varies nearly fourfold across target contrasts and anatomical regions. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/genmilab/PRIMED}.

figures.caption:
\textbf{Pipeline overview.} The three acquired contrasts are mapped by a fixed Haar transform $W$ and
averaged into the informed prior $g(c)$. One pass of $v_\theta$, conditioned on an embedding of the target
contrast, returns the displacement $\hat{D}$, and subtracting it before inverting $W$ gives the volume. \textbf{Top}: the
full bridge path from $s=1$ to $s=0$; \M\ evaluates the network only at the source endpoint, $s=1$.}
